title: Can You Export Customer Feedback Themes Into Excel, PowerPoint, or Your BI Tool?
summary: Thematic exports customer feedback themes to Excel, PowerPoint, PNG, and BI tools like Tableau and Power BI. Five export paths, and who each serves.
body_markdown:
The analysis is the easy part now. The hard part is what comes next. A regional director who'll never log into your feedback platform needs to know what her customers are complaining about, and she needs it in a format she can drop into Monday's deck.


Yes, Thematic exports themes into Excel, PowerPoint, and business intelligence (BI) tools. It does that through five separate paths rather than one generic download button: a CSV of analyzed responses, an Excel file of chart data broken out by theme, an editable PowerPoint report, PNG chart exports, and an Export Assistant that builds a custom table from your filters. Two programmatic paths sit alongside them. Thematic's application programming interface (API) returns CSV and JSON. Thematic also pushes structured theme-level data into Snowflake, BigQuery, and BI tools including Tableau, Power BI, and Looker.


There are five and not one because "export" means something different to an analyst, a stakeholder, and a data engineer. Here's what each path contains, who it serves, and how to test any platform's export story before you sign.


Export path What it contains Who it serves


CSV of responses Analyzed free-text columns plus response metadata such as a net promoter score (NPS), date, or customer segment The analyst joining feedback themes to other data


Excel of chart data Volume, Impact, or average Score for each base theme and sub-theme The stakeholder who wants to sort, pivot, and check the math


PowerPoint report Editable summary of the data plus detail on the selected base theme Whoever is presenting the readout


PNG chart export Volume, Impact, Score, and Comparison charts with labels, comment counts, and applied filters shown Anyone dropping a chart into a document


Export Assistant A custom CSV table built from your filters, metrics, rows, and grouping The analyst who needs a specific cut, not a fixed report


API and warehouse push CSV and JSON via API; structured theme-level data into Snowflake, BigQuery, and BI tools Data engineers and recurring reporting


## What "export" actually means in feedback analysis


Export means getting theme-level results out of the analytics platform and into the tool where the decision gets made. It isn't the same thing as a dashboard, and treating the two as interchangeable is the most common mistake in evaluation.


Four dimensions separate a useful export from a useless one:


- **Row-level or aggregate.** Do you get individual comments with their theme tags, or the rolled-up counts per theme?
- **Data or artifact.** A CSV is data someone will analyze further. A slide is something someone will present.
- **Static or refreshing.** A downloaded file is a snapshot. A warehouse push keeps updating.
- **Themes or just text.** An export that carries the raw verbatims but drops the theme structure has thrown away the analysis.


That last one is the tell. Plenty of tools will export your comments. Far fewer export the themes, the sub-themes, and the metrics attached to them, which is the part that took the work.


## What stakeholder reporting actually requires


**The format has to match where the reader already works.** This isn't a habit to be trained out of people. Alteryx surveyed 1,400 data analysts for its[2025 State of the Data Analyst report](https://www.alteryx.com/resources/report/2025-state-of-the-data-analyst) and found 76% still rely on manual, spreadsheet work for data preparation, even as 97% said AI tools speed up their daily work. If the analysts building the reports live in spreadsheets, the executives receiving them certainly do.


**The numbers have to survive the trip.** A theme is only useful if the metric attached to it comes along. Volume tells you how often something came up. Impact tells you how much it moved the score. An export that carries one but not the other sends the reader back to ask.


**Filters have to carry through.** Most reporting is segmented by region, product line, or quarter. If you filter in the platform and the export ignores it, you're re-cutting the data by hand.


**Somebody has to be allowed to do it.** Export is a permissions question as much as a format question, especially when the feedback contains customer identifiers.


[TechTarget's reporting on BI adoption](https://www.techtarget.com/data-technologies/news/365530077/BI-adoption-poised-to-break-through-barrier-finally) names the structural reason this keeps mattering. BI platforms are still built for data specialists rather than business users, and users have to leave their normal applications to work in one. Every stakeholder you ask to log into another tool is a stakeholder who might not.


## Where most feedback tools fall short


- **Comments without themes.** The export is a spreadsheet of raw verbatims, which is the input to the analysis rather than the output.
- **Themes without metrics.** You get a theme list with counts and nothing about impact on the score.
- **One format only.** Usually CSV. Fine for the analyst, useless for the readout.
- **Charts you can't move.** The visualization renders in the platform and nowhere else, so somebody rebuilds it by hand in a slide.
- **Filters that don't travel.** The download returns the full dataset no matter what was on screen.


Here's a test worth running in a demo. Apply two filters, open a theme, then ask the vendor to produce both the row-level file and a presentation-ready summary from that exact filtered view. Count the clicks and the manual rework.


## How Thematic exports themes


**CSV of analyzed responses.** Thematic[exports a CSV](https://help.getthematic.com/article/59-how-to-download-your-data-from-thematic) with the free-text columns it analyzed, plus information about each response such as an NPS score, a date, or a customer segment. The column set can be customized to what an organization asks for. This is the file for the analyst who wants to join feedback themes against other data.


**Excel file of chart data.** Thematic downloads an Excel file of the analysis chart data, giving the Volume, the Impact, or the average Score of every base theme and sub-theme, depending on which tab is active. This is the one that goes to the stakeholder who wants to sort, pivot, and check the math.


**Editable PowerPoint report.** Thematic generates a PowerPoint report that stays editable after download. It contains a summary of the data plus more detail on the base theme you selected. It's a starting point for an[executive readout](https://getthematic.com/insights/report-customer-feedback-findings-executive-team) , not a finished deck, and that's the right split. The platform supplies the analysis and the numbers. The person presenting supplies the argument.


**PNG chart exports.** Thematic exports Volume, Impact, Score, and Comparison charts from the Analysis Tools as[PNG files](https://getthematic.com/insights/chart-exports) , with sentiment colors, labels on the bars, and the comment count and applied filters printed on the chart itself. That last detail matters more than it sounds. A chart carrying its own filter context doesn't get misread when it turns up in a document three weeks later.


**Export Assistant.** Thematic's[Export Assistant](https://help.getthematic.com/article/174-export-assistant) builds a custom table instead of a fixed report. You filter by date, score, location, or specific themes. You choose metrics including Volume, Impact, Score, and Sentiment. You set rows by theme, score, date, or location, then group by date or by a segment such as NPS or device. You preview the table and download it as a CSV.


**API and warehouse push.** For[reporting that runs on a schedule](https://getthematic.com/insights/automate-customer-feedback-reporting) rather than a click, the[Thematic API](https://help.getthematic.com/article/48-thematic-api) returns data programmatically in CSV and JSON. Thematic also pushes structured, theme-level data into Snowflake, BigQuery, and Google Cloud Platform, and into BI tools including Tableau, Power BI, and Looker. The difference between pushing structured theme data and embedding a pre-built report is covered in Thematic's guide to[Snowflake and Tableau integrations](https://getthematic.com/insights/snowflake-tableau-feedback-analytics-integrations) .


Four operational details come up in almost every evaluation. Applied filters carry into the CSV, Excel, and PowerPoint exports, so a filtered view produces a filtered file. Exported files are named after the dataset, the filters applied, and the date, which keeps a reporting folder legible six months later. Download rights are scoped per dataset, so the buttons don't appear for a user who hasn't been granted them. Large datasets take longer to prepare before the file is ready.


## What this looks like in practice


[Community Health System](https://getthematic.com/insights/community-health-systems-actionable-insights) is a not-for-profit healthcare network serving California's central San Joaquin Valley. It runs an annual employee engagement survey that collects open-ended feedback from staff across 250 departments. The analysis was never the constraint. The constraint was that 250 department leaders each needed their own findings, in a form they could act on.


The team produced 250 department reports in three days. It saved more than 160 hours per reporting cycle and more than $10,000 per cycle, and cut per-department analysis from about an hour to about 20 minutes. Alexandra Clifton, Organizational Development Partner, led the work, and the reports reached directors, middle managers, VPs, and C-level staff. Each one-pager, assembled in Canva from the Thematic analysis, summarized what people liked, what got in the way of team success, and five recommended next steps.


The transferable part is the shape of the workflow, not the tool that made the layout. The analysis happened once. The output went out 250 times, in the format the audience would actually read. That only works if the analysis can leave the platform cleanly.


At one automotive services company the same principle runs through a BI tool instead. The insights team pushes Thematic themes and their[impact on NPS](https://getthematic.com/insights/link-feedback-themes-nps-csat-drivers) into Power BI, so stakeholders across the business reach the analysis in the tool they already use.


## A buyer's checklist for export


1. Does the export carry the themes and sub-themes, or only the raw comments?
2. Does it carry the metric attached to each theme, including impact on the score and not just volume?
3. Can you produce both a row-level file and a presentation-ready summary from the same filtered view?
4. Do applied filters carry into the exported file automatically?
5. Are exported files named so you can tell later which cut of the data they represent?
6. Can export rights be granted per dataset rather than all or nothing?
7. Is there a programmatic path, so recurring reporting doesn't depend on somebody remembering to click?
8. Does theme-level data land in your warehouse and BI tool in a structure your analysts can query?


## The short answer


Thematic exports customer feedback themes into Excel, PowerPoint, and BI tools through five paths, each serving a different reader: a CSV of analyzed responses, an Excel file of chart data by theme, an editable PowerPoint report, PNG chart exports, and an Export Assistant that builds a custom table. An API and a structured push into Snowflake, BigQuery, and BI tools including Tableau, Power BI, and Looker handle the recurring cases.


Here's the test worth running on any platform, this one included. Filter to a single segment, ask for both the row-level file and the summary a stakeholder could present, then count the manual steps between the analysis and the artifact.
